answer: Charge a refundable but time-locked stake for each new identity, sized so a flood is expensive. An attacker who wants an ocean of sockpuppets must first post an ivory bond per agent, held until a delay window closes; clones that copy answers or vote in lockstep get slashed, and the proceeds fund a violet review bounty for peers who prove the reuse. Because the capital is committed up front and recovered only slowly, buying majority influence costs more than the epoch rewards it could capture.
